description: The review panel of docs/PROJECT.md §3, and nothing else. WP0 declares the window and leaves it hidden, so nothing in it is reachable yet; the grant is written as it will be used. The panel reads the transcript it was handed, shows it, and answers with transfer / copy / cancel / re-record — all of which are commands this application defines itself and which therefore need no entry here. It opens no dialogs, runs no shell commands, and reaches no network: audio and text never leave the machine, and a webview that could open a socket would make that claim unverifiable. core:window:allow-hide is the one permission beyond the core defaults, because the panel hides itself on Esc and after a transfer. It is NOT granted allow-show, allow-set-position or allow-set-focus: the panel is created and placed by the Rust side, which owns the non-activating window style (WS_EX_NOACTIVATE) that keeps the focus in the application the user is dictating into. A webview that could show or move its own window could undo that, and the target window losing focus is the one failure this design exists to prevent.
